recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV recent avg 63.6 ms vs baseline 64.0 ms (−0.6%), latest reading 69.0 ms is an outlier — not sustained recovery signal
Sleep avg 4.5 h (15/14 days <7h), well below restorative threshold
Training readiness latest 36, 7-day avg just 29.5 — in bottom quartile
Recovery balance latest 3.07, but 4-week avg is only 0.8 — indicates persistent load-recovery mismatch
ACWR 0.6 (acute 134 vs chronic 223) — far below safe band (0.8–1.3), signaling significant detraining risk from underload *or* suppressed capacity to absorb load
readiness.guidance: This athlete is physiologically fatigued and sleep-deprived; the priority this week is restoring autonomic resilience—not adding volume or intensity.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and intensity versus last month, with pacing slowing slightly but efficiency metrics holding stable — consistent with forced reduction due to compromised recovery rather than intentional taper.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +35 spm this month — the largest single-month increase in the dataset — likely reflecting compensatory form changes on fatigued legs or shorter, more frequent strides during low-volume, high-frequency micro-runs (e.g., four runs on 2026-07-31).

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s volume would require 55.3 km across 8 sessions (~6.9 km/session) in 15 days — impossible without severe risk given current recovery status (HRV suppressed, sleep debt chronic, readiness avg 29.5); chasing this number contradicts all physiological signals and must be abandoned.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated running economy
insights.body: Sleep avg 4.5 h aligns with latest running economy of 253.5 ml O2/kg/km — the highest value in the recent 6-run series and 10+ points above rolling median (253.5 vs 253.5, but note: recent values include 226.0 and 234.6 — the 253.5 is an outlier spike coinciding with lowest sleep and highest vertical oscillillation (8.0%)

insights.title: Decoupling improved despite fatigue — but only in isolation
insights.body: Latest aerobic decoupling is 4.8% (under 5% threshold), yet it follows a median recent value of 7.11% and occurs alongside a VO2max plateau at 39.0 and zero Z5 work — suggesting improved pacing discipline, not enhanced aerobic resilience

insights.title: Recovery balance is positive today (3.07) but masks chronic imbalance
insights.body: While latest recovery balance is 3.07, the 4-week average is only 0.8 — and last 4 weeks’ TRIMP collapsed from 526 → 638 → 249 → 94, indicating abrupt load withdrawal likely driven by inability to recover, not strategic peaking

insights.title: Z3 dominance increased sharply (43% this month vs 29% last month)
insights.body: Zone 3 now accounts for 43% of training time — up from 29% in July and 31% in June — while Z1/Z2 dropped from 48% to 41%, suggesting unintentional 'grey zone' drift that impairs both endurance development and recovery

recommendations.action: Complete two 30-minute Zone 1 walks (HR ≤115 bpm) on Tuesday and Thursday — no running, no cadence target, focus only on nasal breathing and HR stability
recommendations.reason: HRV remains suppressed (63.6 ms avg) and resting HR is trending downward (50.5 vs baseline 51.3) — indicating parasympathetic withdrawal; low-intensity movement supports vagal tone without cardiac stress

recommendations.action: Prioritize ≥6.5 hours of sleep on 5 of next 7 nights — use Body Battery data to anchor bedtime: initiate wind-down when Body Battery falls below 45
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt is chronic (4.5 h avg, 15/14 days <7h) and directly linked to elevated running economy and vertical oscillillation (>7.8% in last 4 runs); this is the highest-leverage recovery lever

recommendations.action: Skip all runs above Zone 2 (HR ≤135 bpm) for 7 days — including the long run; replace Saturday's planned long run with 45 min Zone 2 bike or elliptical (RPE 3/10)
recommendations.reason: Z3 dominance (43%) and ACWR of 0.6 indicate accumulated fatigue masked by low acute load — reintroducing intensity before HRV and readiness rebound risks injury or prolonged stagnation

risk_flags.evidence: 4.5 h avg sleep, 15 of last 14 days <7h
risk_flags.action: Implement strict sleep window (22:00–04:30) with screen blackout 90 min prior

risk_flags.evidence: HRV 63.6 ms (−0.6% vs baseline), resting HR 50.5 bpm (−1.6% vs baseline), but training readiness 29.5 — discordant signals indicating sympathetic dominance
risk_flags.action: Add 5 min morning HRV biofeedback breathing (4-6-8 pattern) before rising

risk_flags.evidence: Z3 = 43% of time this month, up from 29% last month and 31% in June; concurrent drop in Z1/Z2 from 48% to 41%
risk_flags.action: Use Garmin ‘Training Effect’ metric to confirm each run delivers ≥0.8 Aerobic TE before logging as productive

weekly_focus.description: Shift emphasis from output (km, pace, zones) to input regulation (sleep timing, HRV response, breath control) — because current readiness metrics reflect system-wide dysregulation, not lack of fitness.
suggested_sessions: Parasympathetic activation session (5 min box breathing + 20 min supine leg elevation)
